item.title: Pope Leo breaks silence on rosary striking his face in Peru, reveals details about cancer: 'Major surgery'
item.description: Pope Leo XIV says his lung cancer was found in a routine check-up with no symptoms, crediting prayer and doctors for his recovery before the Peru trip.
item.content:encoded:
Pope Leo XIV broke his silence Monday after being struck in the face by a rosary thrown by a worshipper in Peru, joking about the incident while also revealing details for the very first time about his cancer diagnosis and major surgery which took place before his recent trip to South America.

The pope, who had the lower lobe of his right lung removed Oct. 13, after doctors found a cancerous tumor, told reporters on the flight home to Rome that he has not fully recovered, but said he was determined to complete the long-planned 12-day journey.

"Just over a month ago, as everybody knows, I underwent rather major surgery," Leo, 71, said during a roughly 45-minute news conference on board the papal plane returning from Lima, Peru.

POPE LEO WELCOMED BACK AS HE DELIVERS ANGELUS PRAYER DAYS AFTER LUNG CANCER SURGERY

"But from the very beginning, I had in mind that this trip had been planned and that I was going to make it happen."

The pontiff credited his recovery to prayer, medical care and personal determination.

"So, with God's help — and I firmly believe in the power of prayer, as I have literally received messages from all over the world — together with a certain personal determination, which I also have, and with the help of the doctors, it proved to be possible."

Despite the demanding itinerary that included multiple flights and appearances before massive crowds in Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, Leo acknowledged that he is still regaining his strength.

POPE LEO XIV SEEN FOR FIRST TIME SINCE LUNG CANCER SURGERY AMID MAJOR RECOVERY MILESTONE

"I must say that I am not at 100%, but I am doing quite well. Stamina is a gift I have received from the Lord," he said.

The pope also revealed that his cancer diagnosis came as a shock after doctors found an abnormality during a routine annual medical examination.

"The initial news came as a surprise. There were no symptoms — I felt fine," he said.

"It was discovered during some medical tests, as part of what you might call a check-up: a routine annual examination that I have been having for many years."

Leo said the abnormality initially appeared as a shadow on his lung before additional testing revealed a tumor.

POPE LEO UNDERGOES BLOOD TESTS, X-RAY FOLLOWING CANCER SURGERY, VATICAN SAYS

"A biopsy then confirmed that it was a tumor," he said, before adding that he had decided to get it done "right away."

"By the grace of God, I remained calm," he added.

The surgery removed the lower lobe of his right lung after doctors diagnosed lung adenocarcinoma, a type of lung cancer. The pope was discharged four days later.

"No further treatment is necessary. However, as a precaution, I will need to continue having these routine check-ups, simply to keep an eye on things, as is normal," he explained.

The Vatican cleared the pontiff to move forward with his South American trip after medical evaluations in late October.

The journey, which began Nov. 6, marked Leo's first papal visit to Latin America. He also holds Peruvian citizenship and spent roughly two decades serving as a missionary and bishop in Peru before taking on leadership roles at the Vatican.

POPE LEO XIV HIT IN THE FACE BY FLYING ROSARY DURING FAREWELL MASS IN PERU, VIDEO SHOWS

It was while riding in the popemobile through huge crowds toward the Mass in Lima on Nov. 16 that Leo was struck near the eye by a rosary thrown from the crowd.

"The affection shown by the Peruvian people, including the person who, with such great faith, simply wanted to offer me a rosary, is something one carries in one's heart — or perhaps in one's eye," he joked about the incident.

"These are experiences that leave a lasting mark on one's life."

"They bear witness to genuine enthusiasm, deep faith, and the desire to receive the Lord's blessing," he added before describing the crowds' devotion.

"Some even tried to get past the National Police barricades. They simply wanted to live, feel, and experience this faith," he said.

item.title: Pentagon sued by The Intercept, Freedom of the Press Foundation over alleged 'blacklist' of news outlets
item.description: The Freedom of the Press Foundation and The Intercept sued the Pentagon over an alleged journalist blacklist, citing a CENTCOM warning to journalist Nick Turse.
item.content:encoded:
The Pentagon is being sued over an alleged "blacklist" of journalists and news outlets maintained by the Trump administration.

The lawsuit, filed Monday by the nonprofit Freedom of the Press Foundation (FPF) and The Intercept in U.S. District Court in Washington, D.C., stems from a July interaction between The Intercept reporter Nick Turse and the U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) public affairs office regarding Iran's attacks on U.S. bases in the Middle East.

After making repeated phone calls and receiving no answers, Turse was warned by CENTCOM public affairs executive assistant Richard Allee he would be "put on a list of people to disregard" if he didn't stop pursuing the story.

"Turse asked for clarification: 'You have a list of people to disregard?' Allee confirmed with an emphatic: 'Yes,'" the lawsuit states. Turse asked which reporters or outlets were currently on the list. Allee replied, 'I’m not privy to give you that information.' Turse asked if it was a secret list, and Allee stated 'it's not a list that we publicize' before hanging up the phone."

FIRED STARS AND STRIPES STAFFERS SUE PENTAGON, ALLEGE RETALIATION AND FIRST AMENDMENT VIOLATION

Turse later reported in August that he had spoken with an unnamed U.S. official who told him that the office of Secretary of War Pete Hegseth "had a standing order not to engage with" him, according to the lawsuit.

In August, both Turse and FPF filed Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests to seek Pentagon documents pertaining to journalists and news organizations who are on the alleged "blacklist." CENTCOM has not responded to the requests, according to the lawsuit.

The suit accuses the Pentagon of two counts of "unlawful withholding of agency records by statutory deadline."

PRESS FREEDOM GROUPS THAT BLASTED TRUMP TURN FIRE ON DEM GOVERNOR OVER ALLEGED MEDIA RETALIATION

Lauren Harper, FPF's Ellsberg chair on government secrecy who filed the FOIA request on the group's behalf, told Fox News Digital that allegations of blacklisted reporters "should concern both sides of the political aisle, because the tactics that may be used to silence left-leaning outlets today, could be turned on right-leaning ones tomorrow."

"The Pentagon’s budget is at an all-time high, and taxpayers have a right to know how that money is being spent — especially when questions arise about the legality of its operations and potentially dangerous living conditions of its troops," Harper said. "It is the job of an independent press to ask tough questions about these issues and more, regardless of who is in the White House or who runs the Pentagon."

Turse called the existence of a journalist blacklist "fundamentally un-American."

"The Pentagon is keeping vital information secret from Congress and the public — including the true toll of the Iran War," Turse told Fox News Digital. "The American people have a right to know how many service members and civilians have been injured or killed. They also deserve to know the economic costs of the conflict. But the public isn't getting answers because the Pentagon stonewalls and obfuscates. They didn’t want to answer hard questions, so they threatened to blacklist me." 

"If they can do it to me, they can do it to other journalists who demand the truth," he added. "This is a disservice to military personnel and the wider public. If the Defense Department won’t come clean about the war, we’ll compel them in court." 

NEW YORK TIMES BLASTS ‘ABUSIVE’ TRUMP SUBPOENAS TARGETING REPORTERS’ SOURCES

CENTCOM previously denied having a blacklist and called Turse’s account "a complete misrepresentation of exchanges that occurred." It also accused him of repeatedly harassing its staff.

A spokesperson for the Pentagon declined to comment to Fox News Digital. The Intercept did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

item.title: Antonio Sabàto Jr and Virginia Madsen’s son bails himself out of jail after fatal hit-and-run in Alaska
item.description: Jack Sabàto, son of Antonio Sabàto Jr. and Virginia Madsen, posted $5,000 bail after an Anchorage hit-and-run that killed Carl Simmonds, police said.
item.content:encoded:
Antonio Sabàto Jr. and Virginia Madsen’s son, Jack Sabàto, has bailed himself out of jail after being arrested in an Alaska hit-and-run that resulted in a fatality.

In court records reviewed by Fox News Digital, Jack paid bond of $5,000 Nov. 13 and was released Monday.

The 32-year-old was reportedly released under strict conditions prohibiting him from driving, sitting in the driver’s seat of a vehicle and possessing car keys, according to Page Six.

ANTONIO SABATO JR AND VIRGINIA MADSEN'S SON ARRESTED IN FATAL HIT-AND-RUN

Jack was arrested Nov. 9 on charges of leaving an accident without assisting the injured and leaving an accident resulting in injury or death, according to the Anchorage Police Department.

Police identified the victim as Carl Simmonds, 42, who was pronounced dead after officers and medics responded to reports of an unresponsive man near Airport Heights Drive and Debarr Road around 5:48 a.m. A preliminary investigation indicated a vehicle struck Simmonds and fled, police said.

FORMER PENN STATE FOOTBALL PLAYER FACES LIFE-ALTERING INJURIES AFTER HIT-AND-RUN CRASH THAT KILLED HIS FIANCÉE

According to court records obtained by Fox News Digital, Jack faces a felony charge of leaving an accident without helping the victim and a misdemeanor charge of leaving an accident involving injury or death.

Charging documents reviewed by Alaska Public Media reported that responding officers found Simmonds' body on the sidewalk off Airport Heights Drive and several car parts scattered around.

While reviewing security footage from a nearby bank, officers saw a white Chevy Tahoe striking Simmonds and not braking before or after the crash, according to the outlet.

After running the vehicle’s description into the Alaska Public Safety Information Network, law enforcement found the matching vehicle, which is registered to Jack, parked at the Anchorage Amazon warehouse. The vehicle was seized.

According to the charging documents, Jack told police he struck "something" while driving home after delivering for DoorDash, damaging his headlights. He said he believed he hit an animal and didn’t stop because he was driving without insurance. He also said he ran a red light because he felt unsafe driving without headlights.

He said he planned to report the crash after work but contacted police after his girlfriend told him his SUV had been seized, saying he "knew the worst," according to the documents.

item.title: White House pulls Trump’s FDA pick Heidi Overton on eve of Senate panel vote
item.description: President Donald Trump's FDA pick Heidi Overton saw her nomination pulled one day before a Senate committee vote, a White House official confirmed.
item.content:encoded:
The White House pulled Heidi Overton’s nomination to lead the Food and Drug Administration, a White House official confirmed to Fox News, one day before a Senate committee vote.

President Donald Trump hailed Overton as a "ROCKSTAR" in August when he picked the physician and White House adviser to succeed Marty Makary, who resigned in May. 

At her September confirmation hearing, Overton clashed with Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., as he pressed her to endorse universal healthcare as a human right.

item.title: Kim Jong Un's daughter hits ski slopes in rare photos as North Korean dictator tours mountain resort
item.description: Kim Jong Un watched from a throne-like chair, cigarette in hand, as his daughter Kim Ju Ae skied down a snowy North Korean resort during a family outing.
item.content:encoded:
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un was photographed sitting in an ornate, throne-like armchair in the middle of a snowy ski resort while his daughter, viewed as his likely successor, carved down the slopes during an unusual family outing.

The striking images, released Monday by North Korean state media, show Kim wearing sunglasses and dress shoes while seated in the elaborate upholstered chair, holding a lit cigarette.

Other photographs show his daughter skiing in an all-white outfit as officials navigate the slopes nearby.

The girl, believed to be named Kim Ju Ae, has increasingly appeared alongside her father at high-profile public events. 

South Korea's National Intelligence Service has assessed that she is being positioned as his likely successor, although North Korea has not publicly confirmed a succession plan.

TRUMP ARRIVES IN PHILIPPINES AHEAD OF XI JINPING SUMMIT IN CHINA AFTER GOP MIDTERM LOSSES

The snowy spectacle unfolded just as President Donald Trump raised the possibility that Kim could make an unexpected appearance during his upcoming high-stakes meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

"We might have Kim Jong Un. He may come, I don't know. That's up to President Xi," Trump told reporters Monday.

TRUMP’S ASIA TRIP TAKES ALASKA DETOUR AS WEATHER FORCES REFUELING STOP CHANGE

The photographs were taken during Kim's Nov. 15–16 inspection of a tourist zone under development in Samjiyon, a mountainous city in northern North Korea, according to a report by the state-run Pyongyang Times reviewed by Fox News Digital.

Kim visited a ski resort under construction near Mount Pukphothae, where he examined skiing tracks and equipment and instructed officials to prepare the facilities for operation, the outlet reported.

His daughter was photographed skiing at the tourist zone on Nov. 15, according to an Associated Press caption accompanying the government-provided images.

The North Korean leader's visit was part of a broader effort to transform Samjiyon into a year-round mountain tourism destination, with plans for hotels, ski facilities, railway connections and an expanded airport.

TRUMP PLAYS NUCLEAR POKER WITH KIM JONG UN — BUT WHO HOLDS THE CARDS?

The appearance of Kim's daughter added another layer of intrigue to the ski resort visit.

South Korean intelligence officials have pointed to her increasingly prominent public role as evidence that she may eventually inherit power from her father. In an October 2026, assessment reported by KBS World, the National Intelligence Service said her position as a potential successor was strengthening.

The agency has also noted her frequent appearances at military-related events, although the North Korean government has made no formal announcement identifying her as the country's next leader.

The latest photographs offered a different setting for the young girl, showing her navigating a groomed ski slope rather than accompanying her father at an official event.

Meanwhile, the possibility of renewed diplomacy between Trump and Kim remains uncertain.

Trump and Kim last met in 2019, when their summit in Hanoi ended without an agreement on North Korea's nuclear program. Efforts to restart negotiations have since stalled as Pyongyang has continued developing its nuclear and missile capabilities.

A U.S. official told ABC News last week that no engagement with North Korea was planned during Trump's Asia trip, according to Fox News Digital's previous reporting.

Fox News Digital's Alec Schemmel contributed to this reporting.

item.title: 'Mob Wives' star Renee Graziano rejects NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani as 'not my choice' in public safety clash
item.description: Former "Mob Wives" star Renee Graziano criticized NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani and criminal justice policies on Tomi Lahren's podcast, as Mamdani defended his NYPD overhaul.
item.content:encoded:
Former "Mob Wives" star Renee Graziano criticized New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani during a discussion on public safety, saying he is "not my choice."

Speaking on the "Tomi Lahren Is Fearless" podcast, Graziano told Lahren that Americans shouldn’t be attacked for wanting their streets to be safe and said she disagrees with Mamdani on "probably everything."

"I don't agree with him on a lot of things. Probably everything, I don't agree with him," Graziano said. "He's not my choice. And if he is for other people, God bless them. He would not be the person I voted for."

Graziano’s comments came after Lahren raised concerns about New York’s no-cash bail policies and Mamdani’s move to disband the NYPD’s protest unit.

Under changes announced by Mamdani and NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch on Monday dissolving the Strategic Response Group (SRG), the unit’s counterterrorism functions will be folded into the Intelligence and Counterterrorism Bureau, while a new civilian-led Community Dialogue and De-escalation Division (CDDD) and specialized NYPD teams will handle protest response.

MICHAEL RUIZ: NEW YORK'S GUTTED POLICE UNIT WAS MORE THAN A PROTEST SQUAD

Graziano, who said she tries "not to pay attention" to Mamdani, criticized the justice system, arguing that criminal justice policies have allowed repeat offenders to be released.

"You're letting men out that raped women, and they get out and they rape women. They're out the door 20 seconds later, and they're still committing crimes," she said.

Graziano said she’s faced criticism on social media for calling for public safety, including being labeled "MAGA" by commenters.

"I had made a statement. One day on my Instagram, I said, ‘Can we make America safe again?’ And I got attacked viciously," Graziano said.

"‘Oh, you're a MAGA, you're this, you're that, you're Trumper,’ or you're this or that," Graziano added. "First of all, who I decide to pick is my business. I don't need to tell anybody, it's my choice. But I would never attack a person because they don't like this color or they don't like that. I would never do that. And I've experienced that across the board. And all I said was make it safe. I didn't say make it great. I said, make it safe."

JIM CAVIEZEL SAYS A SURREAL ENCOUNTER WITH JESUS CONVINCED HIM TO STAR IN 'THE PASSION OF THE CHRIST'

Graziano also argued that Americans need to be fully committed to the country, saying those who don't want to be here "can leave."

"You know, don’t half step in America. We are America. We are a beautiful country. So either we're all in or we're out. And if you don't want to be here, you can leave. That's how I truly feel."

At a news conference Tuesday, Mamdani defended his decision to dissolve the SRG, describing counterterrorism and protest response as "fundamentally different responsibilities."

MAMDANI PREPARES TO FULFILL PROMISE TO AXE NYPD UNIT RESPONSIBLE FOR CONTROLLING PROTEST VIOLENCE

"New Yorkers exercising their constitutional right to protest should not be met with the same police response as a terrorism threat. I made this promise over the course of the campaign, and I'm proud to be fulfilling this promise," Mamdani said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Mamdani's team for comment but did not immediately hear back.

Fox News Digital’s Anders Hagstrom contributed to this report.

item.title: Trump administration permanently pulls funding from LA homeless agency over mounting fraud allegations
item.description: The Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority will give up about $150 million in federal funding under a HUD settlement, with LA County managing the money.
item.content:encoded:
The Trump administration on Monday announced a landmark settlement to permanently cut the scandal-plagued Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority (LAHSA) off from federal funding, citing overwhelming evidence of fraud and years of mismanagement that wasted taxpayer dollars.

The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) said the agreement requires LAHSA to relinquish about $150 million in federal funding and permanently sever its ties to HUD's homelessness funding programs by the end of 2027.

"Organizations that are complicit in this fraud and waste will not get one penny more of federal funding," Bill Essayli, first assistant U.S. attorney for the Central District of California, said in a statement.

LA HOMELESSNESS FRAUD CASES EXPOSE DEEPER PROBLEM THAN STOLEN MILLIONS, OVERSIGHT HAWK WARNS

Los Angeles County will take over managing the funds used to combat homelessness, while HUD will closely monitor how the money is spent, according to officials.

The agreement, executed Thursday, resolves a lawsuit filed by LAHSA challenging HUD's June decision to suspend further funding to the agency.

According to HUD, investigators found that LAHSA received more federal homelessness funding than any other jurisdiction in the nation, taking in nearly $1 billion in taxpayer dollars over the last five years.

LA REAL ESTATE VET COMES AT MAYOR BASS WITH RECEIPTS OVER DAMNING HOMELESSNESS REPORT: 'SHE DOESN'T GET IT'

"Los Angeles remains the epicenter of the nation’s drug-fueled homelessness crisis. On top of this, their failure has enabled record homelessness fraud," HUD said.

HUD Secretary Scott Turner said LAHSA had spent years funneling federal funding to organizations without proper oversight.

"Taxpayers will no longer bankroll an organization that fails to deliver for the Americans it was created to serve," Turner said in a statement.

HUD’S HOMELESSNESS REFORMS PUT HUMAN LIVES AHEAD OF HOUSING BUREAUCRACY

"For years, American taxpayers have been sending billions of dollars to Los Angeles to house the homeless and other vulnerable Americans. The result? Fraud and corruption," Scott Brady, executive director of the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, added in a statement.

HUD added that it is committed to ending what it called the "harmful" "Housing First" policy, which provides permanent housing to homeless individuals without requiring them to meet preconditions such as sobriety or participation in therapy.

Under a new Treatment First approach, individuals will likely need to participate in addiction or mental health treatment and demonstrate progress toward recovery to qualify for and maintain housing assistance.

"HUD is rejecting the addiction-fueled depravity seen from LA’s Skid Row to New York’s ‘Boulevard of Broken Dreams’ and moving to Treatment First to restore lives of self-sufficiency," Turner previously said.

The settlement comes as HUD reports a 6.3% decrease in homelessness, the largest recorded decline, during the first year of Trump's administration.

"President Trump’s actions to secure the border, get criminal illegals off our streets and restore safety to our communities drove a historic decrease in homelessness," Turner previously said.

item.title: Variety recommends trans actress Hunter Schafer as next Bond girl alongside Robert Pattinson
item.description: Variety recommended trans "Euphoria" star Hunter Schafer as the next Bond girl opposite new 007 Robert Pattinson, saying the casting would "make history."
item.content:encoded:
Variety recommended transgender actress Hunter Schafer as a potential Bond girl opposite Robert Pattinson in the upcoming James Bond film on Monday, suggesting the casting could "make history."

After the "Twilight" series and "The Batman" star was announced as the latest actor to take over the role of 007, Variety published a list of 19 actresses who could play his love interest. 

The list included established Hollywood stars such as Emily Blunt and Margot Robbie, along with newer faces such as "One Battle After Another" actress Chase Infiniti and "Obsession" star Inde Navarrette.

Schafer was the only transgender actor on the list, and Variety's writers highlighted her as a potential standout.

ROBERT PATTINSON NAMED NEXT JAMES BOND

"Not only would Hunter Schafer make history as the first trans Bond girl, she’d be a damn good one," the article read.

The magazine pointed to Schafer's experience in the HBO series "Euphoria" and her role in the upcoming Prime Video series "Blade Runner 2099" as evidence of her acting credentials and potential chemistry with Pattinson.

"We could totally see Schafer and Pattinson sharing flirty banter before going head-to-head against some baddies — and just imagine the looks on that press tour!" Variety added.

IDRIS ELBA REJECTS 'WOKE' JAMES BOND CASTING PUSH, WARNS AUDIENCES 'WON'T GO FOR A BLACK MALE' IN THE ROLE

Fox News Digital reached out to Amazon MGM Studios for comment but did not immediately receive a response. 

Pattinson's casting followed years of anticipation after Daniel Craig's appearance as Bond in 2021's "No Time to Die." During that period, commentators proposed casting an actor of color or a woman as 007.

The announcement of Pattinson's casting, surprised longtime franchise fans, including Fox News contributor Raymond Arroyo.

"As a huge fan of the Ian Fleming novels, Pattinson isn’t quite what I envisioned or what I think fans were hoping for," Arroyo told Fox News Digital. 

"After five Bond films with Daniel Craig in the lead, it was probably time to bring back some of the fun and charm that Pierce Brosnan and Roger Moore brought to the franchise.

"But it sounds like MGM/Amazon wants to give audiences a darker, moodier Bond — just when the public is craving a good, old-fashioned escape," he added. "We’ll see if audiences wish this new Bond to ‘Live or Let Die.’"

FORMER JAMES BOND ACTRESS PANS AMAZON FRANCHISE TAKEOVER AS 'ABSOLUTE MADNESS'

In a comment to Fox News Digital, the Media Research Center's Newsbusters executive editor Tim Graham described the article as a result of woke journalism interacting with classic Hollywood.

"They can only turn to this spin when Amazon failed to transform the James Bond character into a black woman this time around," Graham said. "We know what happened when they tried to make the ‘Ghostbusters’ an all-girl squad. Journalists should refrain from telling Hollywood how to remake the classics. But they know Hollywood is woke enough to take them seriously."

item.title: Skydiving injury leaves 24-year-old tourist stranded in Australia on medical no-fly list
item.description: Chloe Lowe of the United Kingdom says a 10,000-foot skydiving jump in Australia left her with a damaged eardrum, an infection, vertigo and a not-fit-to-fly certificate.
item.content:encoded:
A 24-year-old tourist says she's been stranded in Australia for weeks after a skydiving jump severely damaged her eardrum, leaving doctors to declare her medically unfit to fly home.

Chloe Lowe, a resident of Sheffield, United Kingdom, told the outlet NeedToKnow she's been stranded in Australia "for several weeks" after initially arriving in October for a solo birthday trip.

Days before the planned three-week trip ended, Lowe went skydiving and jumped out of a plane at 10,000 feet. She damaged her eardrum and realized that, once the adrenaline wore off, she couldn't hear.

CRUISE VACATION TAKES FRIGHTENING TURN AS PASSENGER IS AIRLIFTED FROM SHIP

She then sought medical treatment and learned she was bleeding behind her eardrum.

"I was given a not-fit-to-fly certificate and put on steroids," the influencer told NeedToKnow, a British publication.

After two weeks of healing, an infection threw another wrench into her plans, leaving her in more pain and experiencing more vertigo, she said.

4 CRITICAL TRAVEL ISSUES FOR THOSE DELAYED AND DISRUPTED BY FAA NATIONWIDE GROUND STOP

"Turns out I now have an infection due to fluid that’s been trapped inside my ear," she said. 

"Every week I’m having to extend my accommodation, not knowing if I’ll be able to go home by the end of it or not."

In a redacted medical certificate shared by Lowe, Queensland Health officials stated that she was admitted to Cairns Base Hospital and is "not fit to fly at this time due to the health concerns."

Lowe described herself as being "trapped on the other side of the world with no way home."

Lowe told NeedToKnow she decided to visit Australia to pay respects to her grandfather, who died while scuba diving on the Great Barrier Reef in 2016.

"This was a really meaningful trip for me, as I wanted to visit the place where he sadly passed away," she said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Fox News Digital reached out to Lowe for further comment.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Lowe isn't the only traveler whose vacation took an unexpected turn this year.

This summer, a tourist took an 11-hour overnight train from Sicily to Rome to fly home after Mount Etna's volcanic activity canceled her flight.

At the start of 2026, Fox News Digital reported that about 600 tourists were stranded on the remote island of Socotra after escalating conflict between the UAE and Saudi Arabia in Yemen shut down flights.

item.title: Pentagon detains senior US Army officer accused of spying for Russians after UK arrest
item.description: Lt. Col. Brandon Tyner was handed to U.S. military authorities after British counterterrorism police arrested him on suspicion of spying for Russia.
item.content:encoded:
A U.S. Army lieutenant colonel suspected of spying for Russia was handed over to U.S. military authorities Tuesday, days after British counterterrorism police arrested him on suspicion of violating national security laws.

Lt. Col. Brandon Tyner, 41, was arrested Nov. 10 near Gloucester, England, on suspicion of assisting a foreign intelligence service and obtaining or disclosing protected information under the United Kingdom's National Security Act.

British authorities previously said the allegations involved Russia, which the Kremlin denied any connection to.

SENIOR US ARMY SOLDIER ARRESTED IN UK ON SUSPICION OF SPYING FOR RUSSIA

The Associated Press, citing a U.S. official, reported that Tyner had not provided information to Russia.

Tyner's transfer followed consultations between British prosecutors, the U.K. attorney general's office and U.S. authorities, according to London's Metropolitan Police.

Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, head of U.K.'s Counter Terrorism Policing, said investigators referred the case to the Crown Prosecution Service, which consulted the attorney general's office and U.S. authorities before transferring the investigation.

RUSSIAN SPIES ORCHESTRATED $40K MURDER PLOT IN NATION’S CAPITAL, US ALLEGES

"These are extremely serious allegations, and our collective response should send a strong message that we will act swiftly and robustly where we suspect this kind of espionage activity taking place," Taylor said in a statement.

FBI Director Kash Patel said the officer was in custody following a joint espionage investigation involving the FBI's Philadelphia field office, its London legal attaché office, British counterterrorism police, MI5, U.K. defense counterintelligence officials and U.S. Army Counterintelligence Command.

"This FBI has zero tolerance for anyone who betrays their oath to the United States or puts our national security at risk. That’s been demonstrated by the 167 counterintelligence and espionage arrests we’ve made over the last 21 months, a 53% increase," Patel said.

Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon, commander of U.S. Army Counterintelligence Command, warned service members against violating their oath to defend the Constitution.

"This case should serve as a stark warning to any service member suspected of violating the oath we all take to protect and defend the Constitution," Stinchon said.

Tyner, who previously deployed to Afghanistan, Iraq and Qatar, served as a senior human resources officer with NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps at Imjin Barracks near Gloucester.

The British-led multinational force, which includes personnel from 20 nations, is designed to respond rapidly to military crises and operations.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov denied Russian involvement following Tyner's arrest, according to the AP.

"This arrest does not concern us in any way," Peskov said Nov. 11. "We don’t know what it’s connected to. We have nothing to do with this."

British police said Tyner's arrest was unrelated to other ongoing counterterrorism investigations.

According to a Nov. 13 statement from the U.S. Army, Tyner entered active-duty service in January 2008 and deployed to Afghanistan from December 2013 to December 2014, Qatar from July 2016 to July 2017, and Iraq from December 2019 to July 2020.

item.title: Paige Spiranac leaves it all on the field, and little to the imagination, while asking NFL fans tough question
item.description: Paige Spiranac showcases a new NFL collection for Swag Golf while asking fans which team is their favorite, revealing her Steelers and Bills roots.
item.content:encoded:
There's a lot going on when Paige Spiranac drops new social media content. It's often written off as one-dimensional, but nothing could be further from the truth.

Sometimes her content is educational. Sometimes she's asking a tough question. Sometimes she does both. Most of the time her content is conversational.

There's a back-and-forth taking place that requires, at times, several views to fully grasp. Tuesday she asked NFL fans a tough question.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

I admit, this doesn’t appear to be a tough question at all. She's showcasing a new NFL collection for Swag Golf while asking, "Which team is your favorite?"

All you have to do is state the name of your favorite team and off you go about your day. That is until about the third time you watch it.

What if your team isn't one of the handful Paige goes through in the video? Does it now become a question about which team of the ones she has shown is your favorite?

PAIGE SPIRANAC GIVES PEOPLE WHAT THEY DIDN'T KNOW THEY NEEDED: HER YOGURT BOWL RECIPE

By the time you figure that out, you're a half a dozen or more views in. Your mind is in a pretzel, and you try to straighten yourself back out by watching it a couple more times.

You then realize you're in too deep to turn around. You need to decide which way to go. Another time through to help you decide what you should do and, ultimately, you go with your gut.

And for everyone, that answer is going to be different. That's how Paige Spiranac asks the tough questions. She left it all out on the field on Tuesday.

As for Paige, she's supported multiple teams. Though, she has her favorites.

"Both my parents are from Pittsburgh so I was born a Steelers fan," she told her followers. "Can’t forget about my love for the Bills tho."

item.title: Steelers star says international games 'freak me out' after Aidan Hutchinson's injury in Germany
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers star Cameron Heyward said international games "freak me out" over field concerns after Aidan Hutchinson's brutal injury in Germany.
item.content:encoded:
If Pittsburgh Steelers star Cameron Heyward never played a game outside the United States again, he would be OK with it.

Heyward was asked about Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson’s brutal season-ending injury he suffered during a sack celebration in Germany on Sunday. The four-time All-Pro referenced how New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye got hurt on the same play.

"I don't like to, you know, those international games freak me out just because of that. It's just, those fields are a little bit different. It's wild to see," Heyward said during an appearance on "The Rich Eisen Show."

Hutchinson sacked Drake Maye, who may have suffered a season-ending ankle injury on the play, and jumped into the air to celebrate. When he landed, he grabbed his right knee and crumpled to the ground at Allianz Arena, home to FC Bayern Munich.

The seven-time Pro Bowler said he feels horrible for Hutchinson.

"Oh man, that was, as a defender, you're like, I get the sack, and then you go to celebrate, and I'm always wary about jumping in there 'cause there's freaky stuff that happens. But you know, I, I feel horrible for the kid. I got a chance to meet Aiden years ago; we were doing a Super Bowl commercial, and he's one of the nicest dudes, and a lot of respect for his family," Heyward said.

Losing Hutchinson is a major blow to the Lions' defense , which is currently without star linebacker Jack Campbell after he suffered a terrifying neck injury last month.

In nine games, Hutchinson has recorded 24 tackles and six sacks. While the Lions are 7-2 and sit atop the NFC North, the Minnesota Vikings and Chicago Bears are also 7-2. The fourth-place Green Bay Packers are 6-4.

In such a competitive division, the Lions were relying on Hutchinson to lead their defense and help them keep pace.

Heyward would know that playing surfaces are different internationally, as the Steelers played in the NFL’s first-ever game in Paris in October, which they won 16-10 over the New Orleans Saints. The Lions-Patriots game was the final European game of the season.

item.title: Irish boxer Lee Reeves dies at 31 after three months in a coma following Dublin fight
item.description: Lee Reeves died at 31 after emergency brain surgery and a medically induced coma following his 10th-round knockout loss to Gary Cully at Dublin's 3Arena.
item.content:encoded:
Irish boxer Lee Reeves died Monday night at 31. It's a tragic end. He spent the last three months fighting for his life after a bout in Dublin.

Reeves took heavy shots on Aug. 1 in a back-and-forth war with Gary Cully at Dublin's 3Arena. Both guys landed big punches all night. Then came the 10th round and Cully dropped Reeves twice to end it.

Reeves stayed down; medics rushed him straight from the arena for emergency brain surgery. The boxer stayed in a medically induced coma and moved back to University Hospital Limerick in October to be near his family. Things looked hopeful for a bit until his health took a turn for the worse after he caught a bad infection over the weekend, and died Monday.

IRANIAN BOXER ON DEATH ROW WINS HUMAN RIGHTS AWARD AS ATHLETES PUSH TO SAVE HIS LIFE

Tributes poured in across boxing on Tuesday, including from Cully on social media.

"What a character and a gent," Cully posted. "It's never been nothing but love between us, champ. Can't really believe I'm writing this, but RIP, brother."

Outside the ring, Reeves served as a soldier in the Irish Army's 12th Infantry Battalion. He also spoke out often about mental health after losing his mother to suicide in 2015. He even competed on "Survivor UK" in 2023.

Inside the ropes, fans knew the lefty as "El Champo." He won five Irish amateur titles before turning pro in 2018. The guy could scrap.

Reeves walked into the Cully fight on an 11-bout winning streak and a pro career record of 16-2 (11 KOs).

Hall of Fame promoter Frank Warren called Reeves "a fine young man and a credit to the sport." Longtime coach Dee Walsh praised Reeves for his toughness in and out of the gym, saying he made everyone around him proud right to the end.

item.title: Kyle Whittingham addresses job security questions at Michigan, makes more headlines with UCLA comments
item.description: Michigan Wolverines coach Kyle Whittingham says UCLA built its stunning rise on 20-plus transfer portal players taken from James Madison University.
item.content:encoded:
The head coach of the Michigan Wolverines is jealous about a bunch of players from James Madison University, who'd have ever guessed it?

This weekend at The Big House matches up two programs with wildly different histories, backgrounds, geographic regions and recruiting success. Michigan, one of college football’s unquestioned blue bloods, against the UCLA Bruins, who for years were a punchline and in recent years have been better known for crowd shots of a two-thirds-empty Rose Bowl than for their on-field success.

MICHIGAN HIRED KYLE WHITTINGHAM TO FIX ITS MESS. INSTEAD, HE’S CREATED AN EVEN BIGGER ONE WITH WOLVERINES

Both teams have first-year head coaches, also with wildly different pedigrees. Michigan hired Kyle Whittingham after decades of sustained success in Salt Lake City with the Utah Utes, while the Bruins grabbed Bob Chesney whose most recent resume looks like this:

It's Michigan, though, with all their immense resources and recruiting prowess, including signing one of the most highly-regarded quarterback recruits in recent memory, Bryce Underwood, that's struggled. The Wolverines are just 5-5 on the season and are heading into Saturday with two-straight losses scoring a combined 13 points. They've lost to Iowa, Minnesota, Indiana, Michigan State and Oregon, and with UCLA and Ohio State looming, there's a reasonable chance the Wolverines miss out on a bowl bid.

For a program with their resources, it's been, well, an embarrassment.

On the other hand, the Bruins head into Ann Arbor as the most surprising team of the 2026 college football season. Under Chesney, UCLA hit the transfer portal and immediately turned the program around. While they've benefited from an easier schedule, they did beat a quality Oregon team on the road, never an easy feat, and held serve against opponents like Wisconsin, Illinois and Minnesota.

One more win guarantees them a spot in the Big Ten Championship game, and effectively secures their spot in the College Football Playoff. It's stunning, to say the least.

Whittingham, in his press conference this week, was asked how Chesney and the Bruins had done it, and gave a, well, interesting answer.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"Transfer Portal. Look at their roster that's built. Man, what, 75% of their starters transfers for this year, and they hit the nail on the head with their evaluations in the portal. They did a great job of bringing in the right guys," he said. "The previous school that the head coach was at, got a lot of players from there. I think they took 20-plus players from there, something like that. And that's really how you do it in this day and age from just overnight, so to speak, is through the Transfer Portal. That's the only way you can do that and have such a marked change from one year to the next is you've got to have a really successful, great evaluation, and just get the right guys in, the pieces to the puzzle."

That "previous school" Chesney came from was... James Madison. So Whittingham's contention here is that UCLA has become a top-5 team headed for the College Football Playoff because they pulled players from... James Madison? Meanwhile Michigan is 5-5 and staring down a losing season with tens of millions spent on Bryce Underwood, Savion Hiter, and a long list of other former top recruits.

He's right about one thing though; nailing evaluations is more important than ever. Chesney clearly has a talent for evaluating the right players to fit his scheme and coaching style, and its paid off.

UCLA is starting a backup quarterback, Ty Dieffenbach, just like Michigan is starting their backup. The difference is that the Bruins' running game is so good and well-designed that the offense can score points anyway. Michigan with Tommy Carr looks hopeless, though Carr's 4/12 for 45 yards line against Oregon might be even worse than hopeless.

That must be tough to hear as a Michigan fan, that your team has struggled to even reach a bowl game because your roster isn't as good as a bunch of former James Madison players.

Michigan's struggles this year have raised questions about Whittingham's future in Ann Arbor, particularly because there's been a seeming disconnect between him and the team. As well as some online chatter that he's checked out on the season and hoping for a buyout.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

"Yeah," he answered to a question about his interest in staying at Michigan. "But I guess anything I say, you can say, ‘Oh, that means he wants to get fired.’ To me, that’s ridiculous. Do I want to continue? Yes sir, I would like to continue. … That might be the most bizarre thing I’ve heard there."

"I don't know who spun it that way, but like I said, you can take anything and spin it any way you want and try to get the desired outcome you're looking for," Whittingham said. "That was not the intention."

Few, if any, predicted that the Kyle Whittingham hire would be such a disaster at Michigan. He was one of the most consistent coaches in the country at Utah, always punching above the Utes' program size and resources. Now at Michigan, one of the best jobs in the country, he's struggled and is searching for answers.

Not every team with a new coach can turn itself around overnight, and it remains to be seen how the Wolverines and Bruins fare in the coming seasons. But no two teams exemplify modern college football and its unpredictability than UCLA and Michigan. Given how this season's gone, would anyone be surprised if the Wolverines pull off the upset?

item.title: Man legally named Captain America charged with murder after allegedly giving victim’s girlfriend chilling note
item.description: A man legally named Captain America allegedly gave a woman a note saying her boyfriend was dead and demanding her money. Police later found the boyfriend dead inside a home.
item.content:encoded:
An Illinois woman giving her boyfriend’s co-worker a ride escaped after he allegedly handed her a chilling note saying her boyfriend was dead and demanding all her money.

Police then went to check on her boyfriend and found his body inside a Peoria home.

The passenger, Captain C. America, 34, was charged with first-degree murder in the death of Khanh Dinh, 63, according to Peoria County State’s Attorney Jodi M. Hoos’ office.

COWORKER ACCUSED OF SLASHING WOMAN’S THROAT DURING RIDE HOME, VICTIM ESCAPED MOVING CAR: POLICE

The encounter unfolded Friday, Nov. 13, when the woman was driving America, whom she knew because he worked with Dinh, prosecutors said.

"While in the car, the defendant handed her a note that said her boyfriend was dead and demanded all of her money," Hoos’ office said.

SUSPECT IN CUSTODY FOR ALLEGED MURDER OF COLLEGE STUDENT AFTER POLICE RELEASED EERIE SURVEILLANCE PHOTOS

The woman managed to get away and call police in neighboring Tazewell County. Officers tracked down America and took him into custody shortly afterward, prosecutors said.

When officers removed him from a squad car, they found the note the woman had described.

GYPSY ROSE BLANCHARD’S PARTNER, KEN URKER, FOUND DEAD INSIDE HIS LOUISIANA HOME: SHERIFF

The woman's account led Peoria officers to a home on North Sheridan Road, where they arrived for a welfare check at about 7:14 p.m., police said.

Inside, they found Dinh dead. A preliminary autopsy indicated he died from blunt-force head trauma, according to prosecutors.

Hoos’ office announced the murder charge Monday. Authorities have not publicly identified a motive in statements released about the case.

America, whose full legal name is Captain Cautious America, was previously known as Mark Anderson. He changed his name about a decade ago because he hoped to run for political office and wanted to stand out on the ballot, according to The Peoria Journal Star.

America remains in the Tazewell County Jail, where Peoria police said he was being held on unrelated charges. A Nov. 14 jail booking entry lists an unlawful restraint charge.
