item.title: Biden addresses infamous 'we beat Medicare' debate moment in new memoir
item.description: Joe Biden's memoir "Promise Me, America" revisits his "we beat Medicare" 2024 debate blunder, arguing polling never showed the performance was fatal.
item.content:encoded:
Former President Joe Biden reflected on his "we beat Medicare" moment from the June 2024 debate in his new memoir,  "Promise Me, America," released Tuesday. He lamented that the moment had become "Exhibit A" that he was "too old to do the job."

"One moment was particularly damaging. As I was finishing an answer on the deficit, I lost my train of thought, saw that my time was running out on the clock, and rushed the final part of my answer by blurting out: 'We finally beat Medicare.' What I meant to say was, 'We finally beat Big Pharma,'" he wrote. "This had been a huge accomplishment in my administration. As part of the Inflation Reduction Act, we had secured for Medicare the power to negotiate for lower drug prices." 

"Ironically, this historic achievement wouldn't lift my candidacy. It would help to sink it," he continued. "What should have been a highlight of the debate became Exhibit A that I was too old to do the job."

JOE BIDEN SAYS CANCER SLOWED HIM DOWN, LIMITING MEMOIR PROMOTION TOUR

Biden accused President Donald Trump of repeatedly lying during the debate, writing, "Yet none of what he said would generate any impression that lasted past debate night. It would be my answers and my performance that would dominate the press coverage and political conversation in the weeks ahead."

"I knew the debate had gone badly. But I knew that debates had gone badly for lots of incumbent presidents," he wrote. "Especially their first ones. I left the stage thinking I would be debating Trump once more before the election was over."

Biden said pundits and Democratic leaders decided the performance was "fatal," but he argued polling immediately after the debate showed the gap between him and Trump shrinking.

"It would take weeks of hammering in the press before the polls started to move downward," he wrote. "By comparison, in the days after losing his first debate with Mitt Romney, Barack had lost five points in the horse race. But the data wasn't the point. The narrative was. And the narrative was bad. There was a consensus that I had lost. Worse than that, there was a consensus that it couldn't be fixed." 

Biden argued that other incumbent presidents had also performed poorly in debates but later recovered. During the 2012 election cycle, Biden wrote, his debate against Mitt Romney's running mate, Paul Ryan, took on a "special urgency" after former President Barack Obama's "terrible" debate against the Republican nominee.

JILL BIDEN REVEALS JOE WHISPERED 'I REALLY F---ED UP' AFTER DISASTROUS DEBATE WITH TRUMP

"What happened to Barack was not unique. Presidents seeking reelection often have terrible first debates that create media firestorms," Biden wrote. "Ronald Reagan looked lost and confused against Walter Mondale, which is why his quip at their next debate that he wouldn't answer questions about his age because he didn't want to exploit his opponent's 'youth and inexperience' was so effective." 

"George W. Bush was caught with a scowling face," he continued. "Barack looked like he didn't care if he won or lost. There's a reason most incumbent presidents have a bad first debate: They're more focused on the country's and the world's problems than on campaigning. Running the country is the most demanding job in the world — and running for reelection means a second job on top of that."

"The difference in 2024 was not that I had a bad debate," Biden said. "Lots of presidents had bad debates. The difference was that every other president was given the chance to redeem themselves in a second debate. As it turned out, that chance would not be available to me."

BIDEN ACCUSES PELOSI OF WORKING 'FURIOUSLY' BEHIND SCENES TO DERAIL HIS 2024 CAMPAIGN

In an interview about his memoir, Biden said he considered his debate performance inconsequential.

"Look, I don’t know anybody who hasn’t made a mistake in a debate," Biden told People magazine. "To me, it was not very consequential. First of all, I thought there’d be another debate, which there wasn’t."

Biden wrote that the debate "didn't feel right from the start," before describing the moment he believed helped end his candidacy. The debate ultimately preceded his decision to exit the race after weeks of pressure from fellow Democrats.

Former first lady Jill Biden said during a CBS News "Sunday Morning" interview in May that she thought her husband was having a stroke on stage during the debate.

"Biden is correct. He was not the only president to have a bad debate performance," Costas Panagopoulos, professor of political science at Northeastern University, told Fox News Digital about Biden's remarks. "Previous candidates did have an opportunity to recover. The problem for Biden was not simply that he had a bad debate but rather that his poor performance reinforced a prevalent narrative that he was ill-equipped to run the country given his advanced age."

"There were concerns about this on both sides of the aisle from the very beginning of the cycle. The debate just put the final nail into the coffin," he added.

item.title: White House blasts 'Trumpcare for All' pitch from far-left El-Sayed who called president 'unserious fool'
item.description: White House slammed Abdul El-Sayed's "Trumpcare for All" pitch, warning the Medicare for All plan would threaten Americans' existing health coverage.
item.content:encoded:
The White House blasted far-left Michigan Democrat Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed's pitch to President Donald Trump to embrace "Trumpcare for All," warning that the Medicare for All proposal would threaten Americans' existing health coverage.

"The Radical Democrats’ socialist proposal for a government takeover of healthcare should really be called ‘Medicare for None’ as it destroys access to the life-saving care Americans rely on daily," White House spokeswoman Allison Schuster told Fox News Digital.

The sharp response came after El-Sayed, who recently called Trump an "unserious fool," posted a 16-second video Tuesday urging the president to embrace the progressive proposal.

BERNIE SANDERS THINKS MEDICARE FOR ALL BILL COULD PASS, 'NOT ABSOLUTELY CERTAIN' TRUMP WOULD VETO

"I think there is a responsibility that we have to engage with [Trump] as the unserious fool that he is," El-Sayed said during a recent appearance on "Pod Save America," according to earlier Fox News Digital reporting.

Despite those remarks, the senator-elect struck a more conciliatory tone in his latest appeal.

"Donald. Habibi. Midterms were rough. I get it," El-Sayed said in the video posted Nov. 17, addressing Trump with the Arabic term "habibi," commonly translated as "my dear" or "my beloved."

"Trumpcare for All. It's really popular. People really want healthcare. You can put your name all over it."

EL-SAYED ADMITS FREE HEALTHCARE MEANS PAYING 'A LITTLE BIT MORE IN TAXES' REGARDLESS OF INCOME

The video featured a mock "Trumpcare" card and an AI-generated image depicting Trump as Jesus Christ, which El-Sayed, a Muslim, referenced while urging the president to embrace socialized, taxpayer-funded healthcare.

"Donald, this is your chance to heal the sick (like in that one AI image. You know the one)," El-Sayed said.

The White House instead pointed to Trump's efforts to lower prescription drug prices, contrasting those policies with the single-payer system advocated by El-Sayed.

"President Trump is focused on taking on the special interests that are driving up the costs of healthcare for all Americans including through his historic efforts to ensure American patients never pay more than those in other developed nations for all prescription drugs, which has already saved Americans well over $1 Billion," Schuster said.

MAJORITY OF AMERICANS BROADLY REJECT SOCIALIST IDEOLOGY EVEN AS FAR LEFT SURGES TO POWER

"The President will continue delivering real results that lower costs and put Americans first, while Democrats push ideas that have devastated economies and ruined healthcare quality anywhere they have been implemented."

The administration also cited a U.S. Council of Economic Advisers' analysis estimating that Medicare for All would increase the federal budget deficit by approximately $47.4 trillion between 2027 and 2036 in the absence of additional taxes or revenues.

The White House also cited a CEA projection that Medicare for All would shift large numbers of Americans away from employer-sponsored insurance and into a new government-run coverage system.

Medicare for All, a sweeping single-payer health care proposal championed by Democratic socialists, would replace much of the nation's private health insurance system with federally financed coverage. Supporters argue it would guarantee coverage, while critics warn of substantial tax increases and massive federal spending.

El-Sayed's public appeal was not his first attempt to recruit Trump to the idea.

During a CNN appearance earlier this month, the incoming senator suggested that the president could attach his name to a universal health care proposal.

"Donald, if you're watching, we can put your name on it. I know you like to put your name on stuff," El-Sayed said, according to a Nov. 10 social media post by CNN anchor Kaitlan Collins.

The unusual overture follows a contentious Michigan Senate race in which El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers.

The Democrat also mocked Trump, Vice President JD Vance and Rogers during his election victory remarks, adding to the contrast between his earlier criticism of the administration and his latest invitation to collaborate.

El-Sayed is scheduled to take office Jan. 3, 2027.

El-Sayed's office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Fox News Digital's Leo Briceno contributed to this reporting.

item.title: Jennifer Sey fights Colorado law that could punish businesses for refusing transgender pronouns
item.description: XX-XY Athletics founder Jennifer Sey is suing Colorado over the Kelly Loving Act, arguing its anti-discrimination law threatens her free speech rights.
item.content:encoded:
Jennifer Sey has a message for the state of Colorado: She doesn't trust you, bro.

The founder of XX-XY Athletics, a company whose message centers on protecting women's sports, is suing her home state over a law she believes could force her business to abandon the very language on which it was built.

The potential consequences aren't insignificant. According to Hal Frampton, an attorney representing XX-XY Athletics who spoke with OutKick, violations of Colorado's anti-discrimination law can carry fines of up to $3,500 per violation, while certain advertising violations can constitute a Class 2 misdemeanor punishable by up to 120 days in jail.

Granted, Colorado hasn't taken any enforcement action against XX-XY Athletics since the law was passed in 2025. And that's a central part of the state's argument against granting the company legal protection while the lawsuit proceeds.

Sey, however, isn't reassured.

SUPREME COURT MAKES RULING ON TRANS ATHLETES IN WOMEN'S SPORTS

"Then why do you have the law? I mean, I don't trust you," Sey told OutKick. "That's ridiculous. That's an absurd answer."

She described the state's argument as a "trust me, bro, defense," adding: "I'm sorry, I don't trust you."

At issue is the Kelly Loving Act (HB 25-1312), a 2025 law expanding Colorado's anti-discrimination protections to include a person's chosen name and how that person chooses to be addressed — language Sey and her attorneys argue could require businesses to use pronouns and honorifics that conflict with their beliefs.

Following arguments Monday before the 10th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, Sey's attorneys are hoping to secure protection before anyone files a complaint.

"The Supreme Court has been clear time and again that Americans don't have to wait to be prosecuted to challenge unconstitutional laws," Frampton, senior counsel with Alliance Defending Freedom (ADF), told OutKick.

XX-XY Athletics isn't exactly shy about its position on biological sex.

ACTIVISTS UNLEASH A 'NEXT WAVE' BALLOT STRATEGY FOR WOMEN'S SPORTS INSIDE DEEP BLUE STATES

Sey, a former national gymnastics champion and Levi's executive, launched the athletic apparel company in 2024 with the stated mission of protecting women's sports. Its advertising and social media posts regularly challenge the participation of biological males in female athletic competitions.

Earlier this month, Sey helped lead a successful campaign for Proposition 134, which Colorado voters approved with roughly 52% support. The measure requires K-12 and collegiate sports teams to be designated male, female or coed, with eligibility generally determined by biological sex. It takes effect Jan. 1.

Sey said the campaign was an uphill battle involving more than 3,000 grassroots volunteers and little funding compared with the opposition, which she said spent nearly $4.5 million.

But even after that victory, she believes Colorado's anti-discrimination law threatens her ability to discuss the issue.

"Given the speech restrictions, how can we even talk about the law itself?" Sey asked. "So these two things are in deep conflict, clearly, and we need to resolve that."

The lawsuit identifies the company's practice of referring to transgender-identifying male athletes by their biological sex. One social media post cited in court proceedings concerned a male athlete competing in girls' high-school track in Pennsylvania. Its message included the words: "When boys run girls' track, they win. And girls lose."

Sey's attorneys argue that Colorado's expanded definition of gender expression could make such statements grounds for a discrimination complaint.

"Simply sitting around and hoping that no one ever files a complaint against them is not a good strategy," Frampton said.

For Sey, the problem goes beyond the possibility of fines or legal proceedings. She believes requiring businesses to use language they reject would make it harder to challenge the very policies her company was created to oppose.

"If we call them girls, then the issue disappears," she said, referring to biological males competing in girls' sports.

In March, a federal judge denied XX-XY Athletics' request for a preliminary injunction, concluding that the company hadn't demonstrated a sufficiently credible threat of enforcement.

The ruling didn't determine whether Colorado's law violates the First Amendment. It meant the company hadn't established grounds for immediate protection while its lawsuit proceeds.

Colorado maintains that the company is exaggerating the threat.

During Monday's hearing, Janna Fischer, an attorney representing the state, accused XX-XY and other plaintiffs of seeking "the extraordinary relief of a broad preliminary injunction allowing them to misgender and deadname anyone with impunity," according to a report by Shaina Cole of Rocky Mountain Voice.

Fischer argued that the 2025 legislation "did not change any substantive rights under CADA. (Colorado Anti-Discrimination Act)" She maintained that the state's Civil Rights Division looks for a denial of service or conduct rising to the level of harassment, rather than misgendering or deadnaming alone.

Sey sees the dispute differently.

COLORADO MOM WHO SAID DAUGHTER WAS SECRETLY TRANSITIONED HELPS LEAD EFFORT TO BAN BOYS IN GIRLS' SPORTS

"This isn't just about me and my business. This is about all businesses. This is about all individuals," she said. "If this law exists, everybody's afraid to speak the truth."

The legal battle comes against a backdrop of Colorado's previous clashes with the U.S. Supreme Court over free speech.

In 2018, the justices ruled in favor of Colorado baker Jack Phillips in Masterpiece Cakeshop, finding that state officials had demonstrated hostility toward his religious beliefs. Five years later, in 303 Creative, the court ruled that Colorado couldn't compel a website designer to create expressive content conveying a message she opposed.

Earlier this year, in Chiles v. Salazar, the justices sided with a Colorado counselor challenging restrictions on certain conversations with clients.

Frampton pointed to all three cases in comments reported Monday by Rocky Mountain Voice.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"When will they learn?" he asked, according to the outlet.

Meanwhile, Colorado's governor-elect, Phil Weiser, has already suggested that Proposition 134 could face changes. Because the measure is a statute rather than a constitutional amendment, state lawmakers can modify it.

"We're going to have to take a look at these anti-trans measures and what adjustments are necessary and appropriate," Weiser said at a post-election news conference.

Sey, who spent two years helping get Proposition 134 passed, isn't particularly receptive to that idea.

"I sort of dare him to overturn the will of the people on his first month in office," she said. "That's not going to be a good look for him, and I'll make sure everybody knows it."

item.title: Reported 'Monday Night Football' booth tension won't derail ESPN's first Super Bowl, network boss insists
item.description: ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro calls the reported Joe Buck and Troy Aikman feud "disappointing" but says the "Monday Night Football" duo keep delivering.
item.content:encoded:
ESPN Chairman Jimmy Pitaro addressed the reported tension between two of the network’s high-profile stars.

"Monday Night Football" announcers Joe Buck and Troy Aikman have reportedly been at odds this season, and at least one heated moment may have occurred in the broadcast booth shortly before an NFL game they were calling.

Pitaro described the timing of the reports "disappointing." He also praised the longtime duo for not letting their professionalism waver and continuing to deliver quality work week in and week out. Buck and Aikman have worked together for 25 seasons.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"Are we happy about the media coverage recently?" Pitaro said this week during an appearance at the Sports Business Journal’s "Media Innovators" conference. "Of course not. It's been disappointing. But these guys are professionals and are delivering every week."

ESPN is preparing for its first-ever Super Bowl broadcast in February, with Buck and Aikman set to handle the play-by-play and analyst duties. Pitaro said he expects the duo’s partnership to continue through that game. "And I fully expect that to continue through the season and through the Super Bowl," he said.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Pitaro confirmed his disappointment when asked whether he was frustrated this was occurring in the lead-up to ESPN's first-ever Super Bowl.

"Yes, yes. Disappointing, don't like the timing, obviously, either," Pitaro said. "But again, they are professionals, and if you watch the broadcast, you're seeing a very high-quality production."

Buck and Aikman both signed five-year contracts with ESPN in 2022, with the deals set to run through Super Bowl LXI. Buck re-signed with the network in September on a six-year, $108 million contract, according to The Athletic.

Aikman was reportedly caught off guard when he learned he would not be included in a package deal with Buck. His future at ESPN remains unclear as negotiations have reportedly stalled, raising the possibility that the Hall of Fame quarterback could become a free agent after the next NFL champion is crowned at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, in February.

According to Front Office Sports, the legendary pair of NFL broadcasters had a heated verbal exchange in the booth before the Buffalo Bills-Los Angeles Rams "Monday Night Football" game earlier this season.

Aikman and Buck will travel to the Washington, D.C., area for the Week 11 matchup between the Commanders and the Bengals.

item.title: Kindle vs. Kobo: which e-reader you should buy before holiday travel, according to an avid reader
item.description: From the 6-inch Amazon Kindle to the Kobo Libra Colour, here's how the top e-readers stack up, based on my 10 years of experience and love of reading.
item.content:encoded:
I remember when the first-generation Amazon Kindle was released in 2007. I was just eight years old, already a bookworm and delighted at the prospect of taking multiple books on a family vacation without the extra weight in my backpack. Since then, I’ve cycled through several iterations of Kindles through the years, including the exciting Kindle Touch in 2011. Then, three years ago, the Rakuten Kobo entered my life, and suddenly I had a choice to make: which e-reader is better?

With years of experience using both brands and 85 e-books under my belt in 2026 alone, I’m here to help you make that informed decision, so you’re ready to cozy up by the fire or board your plane for holiday travel with as many books as you please (without that overweight baggage fee).

After years of testing different Kindle devices, the 6-inch Amazon Kindle is the one I keep coming back to. It’s seriously small and just as light. In fact, it’s thinner, lighter, narrower and slightly shorter than the similar 6-inch Rakuten Kobo Clara BW.

It slips into purses and bags with ease and even fits in the pocket of my Brooklinen bathrobe. If portability is your utmost priority, this is the one for you.

The smaller display does mean less words on a single screen, which in turn requires more page turning. However, the small size of the Kindle is easy to hold in one hand on the subway and worth the sacrifice for a lighter bag when you're commuting to and from work each day.

Its battery life of six weeks on a single charge is slightly less than the Kobo Clara BW.

THE BEST TECH DEALS: $200 OFF HP LAPTOPS, 29% OFF BOSE HEADPHONES AND $450 OFF A 65-INCH HISENSE TV

The Kobo Libra Colour is my most-used e-reader as someone who loves to annotate their reads. I use the Kobo stylus, which is sold separately. This e-reader shows book covers and comic books in full color, which I love visually.

It comes with a pen you can customize to highlight passages, write notes (with an adjustable pen type and size) and even use your e-reader as a notebook through the built-in notes app. There’s a magnetic spot for my pen right in my Kobo case, so I’ll never lose it. 

However, my favorite feature of the Kobo Libra Colour is the page-turning buttons. I can comfortably hold my e-reader in one hand and press the bottom button to turn the page (you can also adjust what each button does.)

On the Kindle, you press the screen itself, which doesn’t feel as satisfying to me. This is a small difference, but it’s caused me to gravitate towards my Kobo more, despite it being heavier and larger.

Kindle has addressed this problem with a case that includes buttons for a few of its models. If you don't want a separate case, the Kindle Click lets you turn the pages with just the click of a remote for all Kindle devices.

Kobo sells a similar remote that lets you turn the page of your e-book hands-free while lying in bed or walking on the treadmill.

AMAZON'S NO. 1 BESTSELLING BOOK AND 9 READING ESSENTIALS FOR YOUR NEXT PAGE TURNER

The Kindle Colorsoft is ideal for comic book, manga or magazine readers who want to enjoy their content in full color.

It has a larger 7-inch display and, unlike the 6-inch black and white version, it has an adjustable color temperature, a waterproof exterior and up to eight weeks of battery life.

Amazon also offers the Kindle Colorsoft Signature, which has double the storage and automatically adjusts the color of your screen depending on the light around you to ease the strain on your eyes.

For over $100 less, the Kobo Clara Colour has the same full color display in a one-inch smaller screen. That means it's slightly more portable, but you’ll sacrifice about two weeks of battery life.

How do the Kindle+ and Kobo Plus stack up on pricing, book selection and library borrowing? 

Kobo Plus lets you choose the proper tier for you, depending on what you read. For e-books only or audiobooks only, you’ll spend $8 per month. To combine both, the price goes up $10 per month.

Kindle+ is one tier for $12 per month for triple the amount of titles and Amazon-exclusive e-books and audiobooks you won’t find in Kobo Plus. However, Kindle+ limits you to borrowing 20 books at a time, while Kobo Plus has no limit, although it restricts offline reading to 15 titles within a 30-day period.

Independent authors might sign an exclusivity clause to enroll digital editions of their books to Kindle+. This means that you can get access to popular and trending indie books on Kindle+ that you won't find on Kobo Plus.

So if you find yourself constantly adding the latest BookTok recommendations to your reading list, the Kindle may be the better choice. If you want to save money and don’t listen to audiobooks, Kobo Plus offers more flexibility. 

Of course, you don't need either subscription to enjoy your e-reader. Both Kindle and Kobo let you purchase individual books, borrow eligible e-books from your local library and download them straight to your device (my preferred method).

However, Kobo has an advantage when it comes to library borrowing. Supported Kobo devices let you browse your library's catalog, place holds and borrow books directly from your e-reader. Kindle requires an extra step: You'll need to borrow the book through the Libby app or the companion app of your local library branch.

For more deals, visit www.foxnews.com/deals

If portability is your main goal, especially for upcoming holiday travel, go for Kindle, specifically the 6-inch model.

If you want color on a smaller budget, pick the Kobo Clara Colour. If you want the same color capabilities and an annotating option, choose the Kobo Libra Colour.

If you’re just starting out, try the Kindle Paperwhite, which often goes on sale for Black Friday, or the Kobo Clara BW.

If you want a subscription to read all the latest, trendy releases, get a Kindle device and a Kindle+ subscription.

If you plan to mostly read library books, choose a Kobo device to browse and borrow books right from your device, anywhere you have a Wi-Fi connection.

Both brands make reading accessible and exciting, so happy reading this holiday and beyond! Use these devices to power through the rest of your year and meet your reading goals. Check out a few recommendations below for your first book on your new device:

"The Nightingale" by Kristin Hannah
"The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo" by Taylor Jenkins Reid
"The Calamity Club" by Kathryn Stockett
"Whistler" by Anne Patchett

item.title: Dabo Swinney should embrace his villain era to save Clemson football, after promising national championship
item.description: Dabo Swinney says Clemson will win another national championship by 2031, but the Tigers sit 6-4 as fans wonder if he can truly turn the program around.
item.content:encoded:
Dabo Swinney stood at the podium on Tuesday afternoon and exclaimed that he expected Clemson to win another national championship within the next five years.

Yes, the same coach who has decided against adapting to the current era of college football that goes through the transfer portal and takes a person admitting that change is needed to succeed.

We have seen this before from Swinney. The Clemson coach is hellbent on turning things around, this time making the statement following an embarrassing loss to Georgia Tech that left fans without seeing a Tigers touchdown.

DABO SWINNEY REACTS AFTER CLEMSON HITS LATEST LOW WITH UPSET LOSS TO GEORGIA TECH: 'NOBODY COMING TO SAVE US'

Simply put, at 6-4 on the season, we are once again talking about a football program that will come up short of playing for an ACC title. Actually, they are so far off from competing on the national level for a CFP spot, that one has to wonder if Swinney can actually turn this thing around at Clemson.

But don't worry, Clemson fans, Swinney is banking on his past actually being the reason why he will have success in the future.

DABO SWINNEY GETS CANDID ABOUT PAST EXPECTATIONS, TRANSFER PORTAL HESITANCY

"We've had 18 winning seasons in a row, and all I can tell you is we're gonna have a lot more," Swinney said on Tuesday. "We've won in every era. BCS. Final Four. 12 team [playoff]. The 24 [team playoff] starts next year and we'll have a bunch of those, too. We've won two national championships in the last 10 years, so we're averaging one every five years, so by 2031 we're gonna win another one.

"That's how I think. I know people don't like positivity, but I do. That's how I believe. My belief is we're going to go finish 9-4. I will believe that until it don't happen, and if it don't happen, I'll fight again. I'm all in. I've been all in since the day I took this job."

Stop me if you've heard this before, like following the 2025 season that saw Clemson finish 7-6, with a 13-10 record over his past 26 games as the Tigers head coach.

He doesn’t like using the transfer portal unless he really has to. Dabo would rather recruit the high school kids to help build a foundation, which is fine if you are ready to put your career on the backs of eighteen and nineteen-year-old kids who are going up against guys with three or four years of college experience.

And, when you ask Swinney whether his bosses are "all-in" with him pushing forward in this era of college athletics, the Tigers head coach told reporters to ask them that question.

Sure, he can put this on athletic director Graham Neff, but Clemson officials are in a predicament when it comes to paying Dabo around $56 million to go away.

But don't you worry, Clemson fans. Dabo made it a point to say that the winning will return after the Tigers get through this current rough patch that has seen other programs across the country pass them by.

I think we got the picture on opening weekend of the college football season, when LSU thrashed Clemson 51-10 in Baton Rouge that felt more like the Tigers being a 'buy game' for his SEC counterpart.

THERE'S A DIFFERENCE BETWEEN COACHES WHO 'CAN'T' WIN A NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP AND COACHES WHO 'HAVEN'T'

"We're gonna win a bunch more," Dabo exclaimed Tuesday. "Coach Swinney's gonna win another national championship. I'm 56 years old. I've got a long way to go. A little rough patch right here, but I'll work through it. You don't believe in me? That's fine. But I've got 18 years of reasons why to believe.

"If you're gonna just judge me and decide whether you believe in me or not based on two seasons, then that's fine. Everybody's got a choice. But I've got a lifetime of experience, and I've got a lot of fun ahead."

Yep, he referred to himself in the third person.

Dabo Swinney should go full "heel" and hit up Clemson donors for a blank check to attack the transfer portal.

Go out and try to spend the same amount of money as others like LSU and Ohio State are doing on a yearly basis for their football roster. Go the Texas Tech route, or at least try.

If Clemson is not going to pay the buyout and turn the page, have Dabo embrace the dark side of a transfer portal route that he has wholeheartedly steered away from over the years.

Dabo Swinney is saying everything that a guy who knows he's sitting in a comfortable spot would say. He is promising to turn things around, and he's making it clear that if Clemson really wants him gone they'll have to pay.

He might have not just come out and said the last part, but his words are speaking louder than actions.

Swinney has run into the preverbal fork-in-the-road.

Now, I want to see him embrace a side of college athletics that he has stayed away from over the past five years.

We've seen everything else with the Clemson football program over the past decade. Why not Swinney going against his beliefs?

item.title: Europe assassination scheme emerges as Iran denies DC 'dirty bomb' plot amid Trump warning
item.description: President Donald Trump warned Iran would pay a price like no other as Tehran's deputy foreign minister called the chemical weapons report a "shameful lie."
item.content:encoded:
Iran on Tuesday slammed allegations that it was plotting a chemical weapons attack in Washington, D.C., calling the claims a "shameful lie" within hours of President Donald Trump warning that Tehran would face unprecedented retaliation if it ever targeted the nation's capital.

Tehran's denial followed a CNN report that U.S. intelligence agencies had uncovered Iranian plans for potential attacks on senior administration officials, including the possible use of chemical weapons or a radioactive "dirty bomb."

The allegations also emerged amid reports of a separate Iranian-linked assassination plot targeting an Israeli executive in Greece and with Israeli security officials believing Tehran aims to target Israelis overseas as the war continues, according to news outlet Ynet Global.

Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister for Legal and International Affairs Kazem Gharibabadi immediately rejected the allegations in a post on X, invoking Iran's history as a victim of chemical warfare.

TRUMP WARNS US WOULD 'DECIMATE AND DESTROY' IRAN OVER ASSASSINATION ATTEMPT

"CNN's claim that Iran plans to use chemical weapons in Washington is a shameful lie and a distortion of history," Gharibabadi wrote.

Trump was asked by reporters Tuesday during the first leg of his trip across Asia about the alleged plot against administration officials and if there was an imminent threat to D.C.

"Well, if there is, they will pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before," Trump said. 

"I hope it's not, but ... we take it very seriously because they happen to be crazy. But this is why they can't have a nuclear weapon, by the way, in case people had any questions."

SENIOR US OFFICIAL UNDERCUTS CNN'S ALARMING IRAN ‘DIRTY BOMB’ REPORT: ‘IT’S NOT NEW'

"Iran is one of the biggest victims of chemical weapons; victims who were targeted with these inhumane weapons with the support of today's accusers, especially the United States," he added.

"The truth must not become a casualty of the propaganda war," Gharibabadi warned.

TRUMP ADMIN THREATENS IRAN WITH 'CONSEQUENCES' AS ALLIES CONVENE AMID THREATS OF POST-ELECTION ESCALATION

CNN reported, citing seven officials familiar with the intelligence, that American agencies had detected Iranian efforts to develop potential attack options against senior administration officials in Washington.

White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said the administration was monitoring potential threats, but that "at this time, there are no credible threats to the homeland."

IRAN COULD MOVE SHADOW WAR IN A DANGEROUS DIRECTION, EXPERTS WARN ON BACK OF TWO POSSIBLE TERROR ATTACKS

Meanwhile, Israeli intelligence reportedly helped foil a separate alleged Iranian-linked assassination plot Tuesday targeting an Israeli executive in Greece, leading to five arrests in Greece and North Macedonia, according to Ynet.

Citing sources, the outlet reported that Mossad gave intelligence to Greek and North Macedonian authorities as part of a joint effort to disrupt the plot.

North Macedonia's National Security Agency announced that authorities had uncovered the plan, with one North Macedonian national arrested in Greece last Thursday and extradited to his home country. 

Four others were said to have been detained in Skopje, North Macedonia.

The alleged plot was directed by Iranian national Edris Jahangiri Mavaneh, whom the agency linked to people associated with Iranian intelligence and security services, including alleged drug trafficker Naji Sharifi Zindashti, according to Ynet.

IRAN TRIED TO ASSASSINATE ONE OF NETANYAHU'S SONS, PRIME MINISTER SAYS

Zindashti is also wanted by the FBI for operating a network that targets Iranian activists and dissidents abroad.

According to the bureau, Zindashti used encrypted, Internet-based messaging applications to hire criminal elements within North America and to murder two individuals who fled Iran.

Greek outlet Kathimerini meanwhile, also reported that the suspects allegedly planned to assassinate a senior Israeli executive working for a company operating in Greece.

Investigators seized weapons, ammunition, handwritten notes and a map, according to the report.

North Macedonia's security agency said investigators also uncovered secret meetings involving suspects in several countries, including Iran.

According to Ynet, Israeli security officials said Tehran considers its war with Israel as unresolved and is looking for opportunities to retaliate through attacks beyond the Middle East region.

item.title: Apple News promoted news from left-leaning outlets 71% of time, yearlong MRC study finds
item.description: The Media Research Center says Apple News promoted about 60 times more stories from left-leaning outlets than right-leaning ones over a full year.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX — The Media Research Center (MRC) has completed its first year collecting data on a trio of news apps and says it found bias against conservatives, with Apple News leading the way.

The right-leaning MRC, which describes itself as an "unrelenting counterforce to leftist bias in America’s newsrooms, broadcast networks, and Big Tech platforms," examined Apple News, Google News and Microsoft’s MSN over the past 12 months. According to the MRC, all three news aggregators favored left-leaning outlets over centrist and right-leaning outlets, with Apple News showing the greatest disparity.

"MRC tracked every top story Apple News, Google News and Microsoft’s MSN promoted for a full year, and the record is damning," MRC President David Bozell told Fox News Digital.

APPLE, GOOGLE NEWS ALGORITHMS SUPPRESSED NEGATIVE STORIES ON MICHIGAN SENATE HOPEFUL EL-SAYED, STUDY SAYS

Over the 12-month period, Apple News, which comes preinstalled on every iPhone in America, promoted about 60 times more stories from left-leaning outlets than from right-leaning outlets, according to the MRC. The findings come despite a warning the Federal Trade Commission issued to Apple on Feb. 11 over allegations of political bias in its news app. 

The MRC found that 71% of the 6,849 stories promoted by Apple News came from outlets rated liberal by AllSides, which rates news outlets for political bias. Only 81 articles, or about 1%, came from outlets that AllSides considers right-leaning, according to the study.

Google News fared slightly better in the MRC's analysis, sharing only 239 stories (roughly 4%) from right-leaning outlets out of 6,317 stories from outlets rated by AllSides, according to the MRC. Microsoft’s MSN featured a higher percentage of stories from right-leaning outlets (13%) but promoted roughly four times as many stories from left-leaning outlets (53%), according to the study.

APPLE AND GOOGLE SUPPRESSED NEGATIVE GRAHAM PLATNER STORIES FOR MONTHS ON THEIR NEWS PLATFORM, STUDY FINDS

"We are putting Apple, Google and Microsoft on notice. Open your curation to public scrutiny, explain how stories get chosen, and give conservative outlets a fair shot at the front page. Right now, you are showing readers a sales pitch for the left. MRC will keep exposing it, story by story, until you fix it," Bozell told Fox News Digital.

Apple News has long faced accusations of liberal bias, and Fox News Digital reported earlier this year that many of the company’s top executives and board members have made substantial contributions to Democrats in various election cycles.

Apple News and Microsoft did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

A Google spokesperson said Google News is not a single static page that’s the same for everyone, noting that results are selected automatically by Google's systems rather than editors. The company said the MRC methodology is "flawed" because it ignores that Google News automatically updates throughout the day and shows news personalized to users' interests and locations.

APPLE NEWS BOOSTS LEFT-LEANING NEWS OUTLETS, SHUTS OUT CONSERVATIVE SOURCES: WATCHDOG
